messages:
alex: Hey team, escalating a customer report — Next.js Edge function using our Node TS SDK intermittently gets 401s only when bundled for edge. Works fine in local Node dev server.

alex: Customer says it started after lockfile update & bundler upgrade (esbuild -> turbopack). They attached a tiny repro. Logs: 
```
[edge] fetch https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -> 401 Unauthorized
headers: authorization header missing when proxied from edge runtime bundler bundle
```

mira: do we know if auth header is being stripped by the bundler/runtime or if package is resolving to a different entry (cjs vs esm)? usually exports map + deep import can cause twin copies.

ben: can you paste package.json + exports map from their repro? also the reproduction steps.

alex: paste from customer: 
```
package.json:\n{
  "name": "edge-repro",
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/inference": "^3.2.0"
  },
  "exports": {
    "./node": "./dist/node/index.cjs",
    "./edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
    "." : "./dist/edge/index.mjs"
  }
}
```
They import like: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference/edge'` inside an Edge function.

sam: aha if their bundler resolves `@redwood/inference` twice (one copy for node CJS, one for edge ESM) the singleton that sets headers/auth may be lost. Also some runtimes strip `Authorization` headers on redirect/forward.

julie: do they see duplicate versions in bundle? ask for `node_modules/.package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock` entries. Also ask for `npm ls @redwood/inference` output.

alex: customer ran `npm ls @redwood/inference` and got: 
```
+-- @redwood/inference@3.2.0
`-- @redwood/inference@3.2.0 extraneous
```
They said lockfile recently changed from npm->pnpm.

ben: can you try repro locally with turbopack? if we can reproduce we should bisect package.json exports. Also check runtime `globalThis.__REDWOOD_SDK_AUTH` or whatever we set.

mira: quick check — share minimal edge handler they used.

alex: handler: 
```
export default async function handler(req) {\n  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });\n  const r = await client.generate({prompt: 'hi'});\n  return new Response(JSON.stringify(r));\n}
```
They confirmed `process.env.REDWOOD_KEY` present, and when running in Node serverless adapter it's used, only edge bundle breaks.

sam: ask them to log `client._transport` or the resolved module path (e.g., `console.log(require.resolve('@redwood/inference'))`—for ESM they can `import.meta.resolve`), to see which entry was packaged.

alex: customer tried `console.log(RedwoodClient)` in edge build and got `[Function: RedwoodClient]` but header attach function was missing. they ran `grep -R "attachAuth" -n node_modules/@redwood/inference` and found it only in `dist/node`.

julie: that suggests their imports resolved to `./dist/edge/index.mjs` which doesn't include runtime wrapper that attaches header for fetch polyfill in edge environment. maybe our edge entry forgot to include auth middleware when built with certain bundler tree-shaking settings.

ben: possible causes: 1) conditional exports incorrect so bundler used node entry for dev but edge entry for prod, 2) bundler tree-shake removed side-effect module that registers auth header, 3) lockfile produced two copies and one copy lost the shim.

mira: repro steps request: can you try the customer's repro with the following commands: 
```
# clone their repro
pnpm install --lockfile-only # or npm ci depending
NODE_ENV=production next build && next start (edge mode)
# or run edge bundler locally via turbopack/esbuild
```
And then run `npx esbuild --bundle` on their entry and examine output for `Authorization` or `attachAuth`.

alex: customer ran `esbuild --bundle` and saw `Authorization` references removed in minified bundle. They also supplied stack trace: 
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')
 at buildAuthHeader (dist/edge/index.mjs:45:23)
 at RedwoodClient.request (dist/edge/index.mjs:102:12)
```

mira: OK escalate to eng-runtime with a small summary: intermittent 401 in Edge builds, likely packaging/tree-shake/exports map causing auth middleware missing. Include repro and bundle output.

ben: probable quick mitigations for customer: 1) pin package to previous lockfile before pnpm migration, 2) import from the node entry explicitly in server (not edge) if possible, 3) add an explicit import to force auth shim into bundle: `import '@redwood/inference/dist/shared/auth-shim';` (not ideal but quick).

sam: @eng-runtime @devx please take a look: minimal repro at https://github.com/customer/edge-repro (private), branch `turbopack-lockfile` — reproduces 401 in `next build` with turbopack.

julie: logging next steps in ticket: (1) ask customer for `npm pack` of their node_modules (2) ask them to try `NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-specifier-resolution=node`? maybe not. (3) engineering to run bisect on `exports` map and bundler flags that drop side-effects.

alex: I'll attach bundle snippets and their package-lock to the ticket. thanks. :thumbsup:

sdk-bot: Note: creating internal bug 2278 — "edge bundle auth shim dropped under turbopack/esbuild with certain exports map + lockfile combos" and assigning to eng-runtime.
